messages:
maria: Heads-up — we're getting a customer escalation for persistent p95/p99 regressions on text-generation routes since the 02:00 deploy. Multiple customers reporting 2-3x p99. I dug into telemetry: huge spike in KV/prefix cache miss rate across serving pool A.

alex: which pool exactly? any correlation with model variants or seq len?

maria: pool A (eu-west-1-gpu-3). p95 went from ~120ms -> 380ms, p99 from ~300ms -> 900ms over the last hour. Miss rate on prefix cache jumped from ~6% -> ~72%. eviction_rate metric also up. seemed to coincide with config change that rolled out a new cache key format at 02:03.

ingrid: that sounds like a cache key bug. do we have example keys? can we repro locally by replaying traffic?

maria: grabbed a few logs. here's an anonymized snippet showing keys:

```
[2026-03-15T02:05:12Z] request_id=abc123 model=redwood-7b seq_len=512 prefix_key=prefix::user::null::model::redwood-7b
[2026-03-15T02:05:12Z] request_id=abc124 model=redwood-7b seq_len=128 prefix_key=prefix::user::client-42::model::redwood-7b
[2026-03-15T02:05:13Z] request_id=abc125 model=redwood-7b seq_len=512 prefix_key=prefix::user::null::model::redwood-7b
```

maria: notice the `null` in some keys — looks like a missing client_id serialization for a subset of requests. that would cause heavy collisions and thrash (evictions & lots of cache fills).

sam: confirmed. our rollout changed `cache_key = f"prefix::user::{client_id}::model::{model_name}"` but when client_id is absent we write the literal "null" instead of skipping or using anon-id. previously we partitioned by client_id via routing and warm caches per tenant, so this introduces incorrect cross-tenant sharing and eviction.

alex: Oof. That could explain both the miss spike and why latency climbs for tenants that used to have warmed entries. what are immediate mitigations?

ingrid: short-term: revert the key change OR patch to avoid literal 'null' by injecting a tenant-scoped placeholder that includes request origin. Also increase cache size temporarily for pool A and reduce TTL to limit cross-tenant pollution.

sre-oncall: I'll do a quick config push: 1) increase cache capacity by 30% on pool A, 2) lower prefix TTL from 8h -> 1h, 3) enable sticky routing to try to reduce cross-host eviction. prepping change now.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered by sre-oncall: changeset/cache-tmp-capacity-20260315 (rolling, 10% batch)

maria: while that's rolling, we should hotfix the key gen to avoid 'null' literal. patch idea: `client_tag = client_id if client_id else request_source + '-' + short_hash(request_id)` so keys remain unique and not colliding.

sam: will open PR for hotfix. Quick test locally with replayed traffic shows dramatic drop in collisions. local metrics: miss_rate down from 71%->8% after applying key fix and warming for 20m.

alex: great. plan: immediate mitigation = up capacity + TTL drop + sticky routing. hotfix PR to restore proper key behavior. rollback only if perf stays bad after hotfix. Also notify affected customers with ETA.

ingrid: add a forced cache-warm job for top-10 tenants while warmup happens (replay stored recent traces with safe sampling). that'll help p99 quickly.

maria: I've drafted the customer update: apology + timeline + short RCA (cache key bug caused cross-tenant thrash) + mitigations. pinging support to send.

sre-oncall: capacity change rolled out to 100% at 02:22. TTL change at 02:24. sticky routing enabled on pool A. monitoring now. eviction_rate is trending down, miss_rate dropping from 72% -> 28% in last 8m. p95 down to ~210ms.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: PR#4321 cache-key-hotfix merged and promoted to canary (pool A canary hosts).

sam: canary looks good: prefix miss on canary hosts ~4% vs ~30% on prod hosts. will promote hotfix to all hosts after canary hold (5m).

alex: after full promote we should run end-to-end smoke against customer traces and verify p99 back to baseline for top tenants. Also add an assert in tests to prevent `client_id` from becoming empty string/null in key formatter.

maria: long-term actions to add to the ticket: 1) guardrail in key generator (fail-fast if critical fields missing), 2) per-tenant partitioning opt-in flag, 3) more granular cache telemetry (per-tenant miss/evict), 4) automated warmup traces after deploy for heavy tenants, 5) pre-deploy static analysis check for caching-related config changes.

ingrid: also postmortem and blameless RCA. add synthetic test that injects missing client_id and ensures it doesn't produce a small set of repeated keys.

sre-oncall: p99 is trending down. current numbers: p95 ~150ms, p99 ~320ms for the affected routes. will keep watch for another hour then close the incident if stable.

maria: thanks all. I'll attach logs & graphs to the support ticket and close the loop once customer confirms latency normalized. :thumbsup:
